To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the critical current density in Bi-2212 round wires decreases away from the ends, and this is directly related to the wire expansion, which is due to the gas pressure generated during the heat treatment, which is a consequence of the melting process.

the internal gas pressure in Ag-sheathed Bi-2210 wires increases with wire length, and that this pressure causes expansion of the wire diameter, dedensification of the filaments and a reduction in the critical current density, Jc.

the critical current density (Ic) in Ag-alloy-sheathed Bi-2211 wires is degraded by length-dependent wire expansion and dedensification of filaments due to gas pressure, which can be reduced by heat treatment below the Ag alloy melting point.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the length dependence of the critical current density (JC) in Bi-2212 round wires.
the development of a new method to control the internal gas pressure and thus the wire diameter and filament density.
the effect of length on the critical current of Bi-2211/2212 wires.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the internal gas pressure generated in Ag-sheathed Bi-221 wire during heat treatment is a major factor in the degradation of critical current with length, and that this degradation can be eliminated by controlling the gas pressure.

the length-dependent Jc degradation of Ag-sheathed Bi-2210/2212 round wires is due to wire expansion caused by the internal gas generated by the heat treatment process, and the expansion can be reduced or eliminated if the internal gas pressure can be controlled.
the length dependence of Jc in Ag-sheathed Bi-2213 is due to wire expansion and dedensification of the filaments, which are caused by the internal gas generated during the heat treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the internal gas pressure in Bi-2212 is very high, and that the wire expansion is length-dependent, and that it is a major cause of the length-dependent degradation of critical current.
, in order to obtain a high Jc in a long Bi-2212 conductor, the internal gas pressure must be reduced by a factor of 2 or more, and that this can only be achieved by reducing the wire length.
Bi-2212 round wires are not yet a mature technology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the internal gas pressure in Bi-2212 tapes is a key issue in the quest to develop high Jc wires.
the internal gas pressure in Bi-2223 wire can be controlled by the heat-treatment procedure, and that it is essential to control this pressure to attain the highest possible Jc.
the wire length is an important variable to be considered in the manufacture and evaluation of Bi-2211 wires.
